docs.title: Release Checklist — kneo-agent v1.2.0
docs.text:
Tracks the next minor release after v1.1.1 (tagged 2026-05-03).

State at the time this file was written: - pyproject.toml version: 1.1.1 - Latest tag: v1.1.1 - CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]: empty - Uncommitted: docs/README.md rewrite + new docs/README-dev.md (mirrors the top-level README split done in 1.1.1)

A minor bump (1.1.1 → 1.2.0) requires at least one user-facing Added/Changed entry. If nothing in Phase 1 lands, this should ship as 1.1.2 instead.

What kneo-agent is. A Python library / SDK — pip install kneo-agent, import kneo_agent. Users build their own application around it (a script, a worker, a FastAPI handler, a Lambda, a notebook). The SDK does not ship a daemon, an HTTP server, a CLI entry point, container images, deployment manifests, or an ops runtime. Anything in this checklist that sounds like "deploy kneo-agent" really means "make it easy for the user's application to integrate kneo-agent." Service-container concerns belong in a separate downstream product (see Out of scope below).

Target audience: small / medium enterprise users, open-source developers, on-premise / self-hosted deployments, and enterprise data-source / service integration via tools and MCP. Prioritization rubric for everything below:

  • SME wins: production reliability, cost control, observability, drop-in defaults, predictable upgrades.
  • OSS-developer wins: clear extension points, low-friction contribution flow, stable public surface, runnable recipes.
  • On-prem wins: works fully air-gapped (no required egress), local / self-hosted LLM support, configurable provider endpoints (base_url), self-hosted observability backends, plays cleanly with whatever container / orchestration the user already has, no telemetry phone-home, reproducible installs.
  • Enterprise integration wins: agents reach internal data sources (SQL, object stores, file shares, search indices) and internal services (REST/gRPC, queues, ticketing/CRM/ERP) via tools and MCP, with credentials plumbed through a documented secret-loading pattern rather than embedded in prompts or tool args.
  • Deprioritize features that only pay off at large-enterprise scale (SSO/RBAC/audit at the SDK layer), single-team niches, anything that hard-codes SaaS-only assumptions, or anything that turns the SDK into a service runtime.

docs.title: What v1.1.1 already gives us (do not redo)
docs.text:
Audit on 2026-05-04 confirmed these are already in the codebase. Phase 1 focuses on new work; touch these only to document or extend.

  • Middleware framework. AgentMiddleware Protocol + four hooks (wrap_run, wrap_stream, wrap_model_call, wrap_tool_call), BaseAgentMiddleware, and composable dispatch in kneo_agent/core/middleware.py:82-206. OpenTelemetryMiddleware ships in kneo_agent/observability/tracing.py:52-95.
  • record_arguments / record_results flags on OpenTelemetryMiddleware (tracing.py:84-85) — partial redaction story already exists; RedactionMiddleware should build on it, not replace it.
  • base_url / endpoint override path for OpenAI-compatible servers via the openai_client parameter on OpenAIAgentsImpl (providers/openai_agents/impl.py:50). LangChain wraps any BaseChatModel so the same path works there. Capability is real; the gap is documentation + first-class factory exposure.
  • No phone-home. Code audit found no analytics, update checks, or metrics egress. Only urllib.request.urlopen use is in kneo_agent/mcp/client.py:23-25 for the MCP HTTP/SSE transports (intentional, not telemetry). [telemetry] extra ships only opentelemetry-api; the SDK does not impose an exporter.
  • RunResult.metadata["usage"] field exists (core/types.py:98) and OpenTelemetryMiddleware._set_usage_attributes() reads input_tokens/output_tokens (with prompt_tokens/ completion_tokens aliases) from it (tracing.py:219-234). Shape is implicit. Other documented keys in the API reference today: metadata["stopped_by_max_iterations"] and metadata["plan"] (Plan-Act strategy). The new formal usage spec should join those, not replace them.
  • MCP HTTP / SSE transports with custom headers (mcp/client.py:70-106, MCPServerConfig.http(headers=...) / .sse(headers=...)). Bearer/JWT auth already works; TLS / mTLS / custom-CA still missing.
  • Issue + PR templates and Dependabot config are present: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/{bug_report,feature_request}.yml, .github/pull_request_template.md, .github/dependabot.yml.
  • Python 3.13 in CI matrix (.github/workflows/ci.yml:55); only the pyproject.toml classifier line is missing.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Decide scope
docs.text:
Pick which to commit to before starting implementation. Each item is tagged with primary audience win and current state from the audit (NEW / PARTIAL → finish / DOC-ONLY). Everything below is a library deliverable: Python API, importable extension point, runnable example, or doc.

Release blockers for v1.2.0 — these must land or the release slips:

  • First-class local-LLM API (Tier B base_url=).
  • Standardized RunResult.metadata["usage"] schema (Tier B).
  • Regenerated API reference at v1.2.0 (Phase 4).
  • Public API compatibility snapshot test (Phase 1.5).
  • Sensitive-data redaction regression tests (Phase 1.5), gated on the credential-plumbing item landing.

Anything else may slip to a later release if not already implemented and tested by the freeze date — keep the bar at "ship something useful, not everything in Tier A/B/C/D."

Per-feature design checkpoint — apply before writing code, not after. For every new public primitive in any Tier-A/B/C item, decide explicitly: 1. Does it belong in top-level kneo_agent.__all__, in a subpackage export only, or as experimental / internal? 2. Document that decision in docs/api_stability.md (the new file from Tier C) at the same time the code lands, not in a follow-up. 3. The API reference section that owns the new primitive must be updated in the same PR (Phase 4 has the regenerate step, but per-PR signature drift is what makes regeneration painful).

docs.title: Tier A — High-leverage, mostly net-new
docs.text:
• [ ] Production-ready middleware bundle (SME + on-prem) — NEW. RetryMiddleware, RateLimitMiddleware, TokenBudgetMiddleware, RedactionMiddleware, all built on the existing AgentMiddleware framework. The redaction one should compose with the existing record_arguments/record_results flags on OpenTelemetryMiddleware rather than duplicate them. Acceptance criteria:
  • Export from a stable public module (e.g. kneo_agent.middleware.*) with documented import paths added to __all__.
  • Document ordering rules for static (constructor-time) vs per-run (RunConfig.middlewares) middlewares; include an example showing deterministic ordering when the same class is registered both ways.
  • Test composition: RedactionMiddleware paired with OpenTelemetryMiddleware(record_arguments=False, record_results=False) produces spans with no leaked args/results, asserted directly from a MemoryExporter.
  • Each middleware ships an examples/cookbook/ snippet exercising its primary use case.
  • [ ] Enterprise data-source tool patterns *(enterprise integration
  • on-prem) — NEW. Runnable cookbook recipes for the common shapes — these are snippets the user pastes into their own application*, not pre-built tool packages:
  • SQL (PostgreSQL / MySQL / SQL Server) — read-only query tool with parameter binding, schema-introspection helper, and a pagination-aware fetch.
  • Object store (MinIO / on-prem S3-compatible) — list / get / put with endpoint_url override.
  • REST / HTTP service — typed request tool over httpx, with a per-host auth header injector.
  • Search index (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch) — query tool.
  • File share — already covered by the MCP filesystem server (example 12_mcp_stdio_filesystem.py); cross-link from the cookbook. Goal is patterns and recipes, not a vendored client zoo — keep third-party deps out of the core install.
  • [ ] Credential / secret plumbing for tools + MCP (enterprise integration + on-prem) — NEW. Small SecretProvider protocol (or documented env-var + secret-file pattern) so credentials reach tool handlers and MCP transports without appearing in prompts, tool args, or trace spans. Pair with the new RedactionMiddleware.
  • [ ] Workflow reliability primitives (SME + on-prem) — PARTIAL → finish. Graph-shape orchestration already exists: the API reference documents WorkflowBuilder.add_edge(..., condition=...) and WorkflowEdge.condition, so conditional branching is in v1.1.1 — it just isn't surfaced as a first-class pattern.
  • Add a retry-on-failure workflow step / wrapper (the genuinely missing piece) with backoff knobs.
  • Decide whether the existing WorkflowBuilder is the public graph builder. If yes, document it as such (rename in docs, cross-link from each *Builder page); do not introduce a parallel WorkflowGraphBuilder that duplicates the API.
  • Add cookbook + unit tests showing conditional branching via WorkflowEdge.condition. Only introduce a new dedicated "conditional step" type if it materially improves ergonomics over add_edge(..., condition=...); otherwise stick with documentation + examples.
  • [ ] Cookbook examples (SME + OSS + on-prem + enterprise integration) — NEW directory, examples/cookbook/, with integration recipes (small Python scripts users adapt into their own application code): customer-support agent; RAG over an internal SQL warehouse; document-extraction pipeline reading/writing to MinIO; internal-API triage agent (REST tool + retry); worked cost-cap example; fully-local stack against a user-run Ollama; air-gapped pip install; end-to-end "enterprise inside the firewall" walkthrough combining local LLM + internal MCP server + SQL tool + object-store tool + secret provider. The smoke test in tests/integration/test_examples.py should pick these up.

docs.title: Tier B — Finish what's already half-done
docs.text:
• [ ] First-class local-LLM API + example (on-prem) — PARTIAL → finish. Currently the API reference exposes openai_client (a pre-built AsyncOpenAI) on build_agent, build_sync_agent, BridgeAgentFactory.for_openai, and NativeRuntimeFactory.for_openai, but no direct base_url= parameter. Surface base_url= (or endpoint=) directly on each of those entry points so users don't have to pre-construct the client. Add examples/cookbook/local_ollama.py exercising it (assumes the user is running Ollama themselves; the SDK does not start one). Document the supported local servers (Ollama / vLLM / llama.cpp / LocalAI) in README and a new docs/local_llm_guide.md. Update the API reference entries for all four entry points to include the new parameter.
  • [ ] Standardized usage / cost metadata (SME + on-prem) — PARTIAL → finish. The current API reference only describes RunResult.metadata as "strategy-specific extras," so the contract is implicit. Write a formal RunResult.metadata["usage"] schema spec in core/types.py docstring and as a new section in the API reference under RunResult, with the matching OpenTelemetry attribute mapping cross-referenced from the observability section. Then audit every runtime — Bridge / Native / Adapter for OpenAI, LangChain, Google ADK — to confirm they all populate the documented keys. Add a unit test per runtime asserting the shape.
  • [ ] MCP TLS / mTLS / custom-CA support *(enterprise integration
  • on-prem) — PARTIAL → finish. The current API reference documents MCPServerConfig.http() / .sse() with headers and timeout only — no TLS knobs. Extend both factories (mcp/client.py:70-106) with verify, ca_bundle, client_cert, client_key parameters. The current urllib.request.urlopen path needs an SSLContext. Update the API reference MCP section* to show the new signatures, plus expand docs/mcp_guide.md with a corporate-TLS / mTLS recipe.
  • [ ] Self-hosted observability walkthrough (SME + on-prem) — PARTIAL → finish. New docs/self_hosted_observability.md showing end-to-end wiring of the existing [telemetry] extra to a user-run OTLP collector → (Jaeger / Grafana Tempo / SigNoz). The SDK exports spans; the user runs the backend.
  • [ ] OSS scaffolding gaps (OSS) — PARTIAL → finish. Add CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant 2.1), SECURITY.md (private-disclosure email + supported-version table), and enable GitHub Discussions; link both from README. Issue/PR templates and Dependabot are already present — leave them alone.

docs.title: Tier C — Small lift, high signal
docs.text:
• [ ] Air-gapped install + no-phone-home doc (on-prem) — DOC-ONLY. Code audit confirmed there is no egress; we just need to say so. Add a "No phone-home" section to README and a new docs/offline_install.md with the pip download --dest wheelhouse/ ... → pip install --no-index --find-links wheelhouse/ ... flow.
  • [ ] MCP server catalog from config (enterprise integration + on-prem) — NEW. Document the recipe for declaring a list of MCPServerConfig entries from YAML/JSON in the user's own application bootstrap (operators want to declare internal MCP endpoints per environment without code changes); ship a tested examples/cookbook/ snippet exercising it. Recipe-only — no first-party config-loader API in this release.
  • [ ] Public API stability tier doc (SME + OSS + on-prem) — DOC-ONLY. New docs/api_stability.md (or a section in CONTRIBUTING.md) declaring: what is public surface (everything in kneo_agent.__all__), the deprecation policy (one minor of DeprecationWarning before removal), and what counts as experimental (mark in docstring + CHANGELOG entry).
  • [ ] Upgrade guide — docs/upgrading_to_1.2.md (SME + on-prem) — DOC-ONLY. Short "should I upgrade?" walkthrough covering: new defaults, the local-LLM base_url= parameter, the formal RunResult.metadata["usage"] shape, any middleware behavior changes, MCP TLS knobs, and any deprecations. Even a mostly-additive minor benefits from a one-page upgrade narrative — most readers won't diff CHANGELOG entries.
  • [ ] Python 3.13 classifier (SME + OSS) — TRIVIAL. Add Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13 to pyproject.toml classifiers (line 19). CI already runs on 3.13.

docs.title: Tier D — Audit gaps to fold in cheaply
docs.text:
• [ ] Streaming-support contract clarity (SME + OSS) — Bridge
  • OpenAI Native + Google ADK Adapter all stream; LangChain Adapter conditional on astream. Document each runtime's streaming status and make supports_streaming() authoritative; pair with a unit test that asserts StreamingNotSupportedError is raised explicitly rather than silently falling back. Doc + small test, cheap.
  • [ ] Sync API guidance — README/API-doc consistency (SME + OSS) — DOC-ONLY. The API reference already documents that SyncAgent uses asyncio.run() and raises RuntimeError inside an already-running loop, calling out Jupyter and FastAPI-style async contexts. README and docs/README.md don't yet repeat this. Copy the existing API-reference warning verbatim into the README quick-start and docs/README.md; verify all three surfaces (README, docs/README, API reference) present the same guidance after the sync.

docs.title: Phase 1.5 — Release-quality test gates
docs.text:
Contract tests and CI guards that protect v1.2.0 from accidental regressions. None of these are features; they're nets. Land them alongside the Phase 1 work, not as an afterthought.

  • [ ] Public API compatibility snapshot test. Add tests/unit/test_public_api_snapshot.py that snapshots kneo_agent.__all__ (and ideally each subpackage's __all__) against a checked-in expected list. Failures force the author to either (a) revert the unintentional change, or (b) update the snapshot and add CHANGELOG + API-reference entries in the same PR.
  • [ ] Middleware ordering contract tests. Add unit tests asserting the documented ordering: static-constructor middleware runs first, per-run (RunConfig.middlewares) middleware appended deeper. Cover short-circuiting (a middleware returning early prevents inner ones from running), exception propagation (an inner middleware raising is observable to outer wrappers), and the same rules under Agent.stream() not just Agent.run(). Lock the contract before the new middleware bundle (Tier A) lands.
  • [ ] Sensitive-data redaction regression tests. Run a fixture matrix of representative secrets — API keys, bearer tokens, database connection strings (postgres://...), S3 access-key pairs, JWT-shaped strings, MCP Authorization headers — through an agent with RedactionMiddleware + OpenTelemetryMiddleware + SecretProvider. Assert none of the secret values appear in: middleware logs, OTel span attributes, exception messages, or any serialized tool-call trace. Block the credential-plumbing item from shipping until this passes.
  • [ ] Minimal-core install (no extras) CI job. Add a CI matrix cell that installs kneo-agent with no extras and runs a smoke import asserting that Agent, AgentBuilder, ToolRegistry, the workflow primitives, MCP types, and the middleware-bundle classes import without pulling openai-agents / langchain / google-adk / opentelemetry-*. Belt-and-braces against accidental top-level imports of optional deps.
  • [ ] Deprecation-warning behavior tests. For every name marked deprecated under the new stability policy (Tier C), add a unit test asserting that (a) using it emits DeprecationWarning, and (b) it still produces the documented runtime behavior in v1.2.0 (one-minor grace period). Cross-link the deprecation in CHANGELOG.md and docs/api_stability.md.

docs.title: Out of scope — not the SDK's job
docs.text:
kneo-agent is a Python library. The items below are valid concerns, but they belong to whatever process / container / orchestrator the user wraps the SDK in — i.e., a separate downstream product (e.g. a kneo-agent-server or an ops-tooling project). Documented here so future scope reviews don't relitigate them.

  • Shipping a Dockerfile / container image / deployment manifests for "the SDK". The SDK doesn't run; it's imported. Containers, Helm charts, K8s YAML, systemd units, and docker-compose.yml files for a deployed service all live in the user's application repo (or a separate deployment product). The cookbook may show a user-side compose snippet that runs Ollama + an OTLP collector for a local dev loop, but that's user infrastructure, not an SDK artifact.
  • An ops CLI or daemon entry point. [project.scripts] was intentionally removed in 1.1.1 (the old kneo-test / python -m kneo_agent smoke runner). Re-introducing a kneo-agent serve command — or any long-running entry point — is out of scope.
  • Declarative whole-agent config from a file (YAML/TOML for the full provider / model / tools / middlewares / skills / MCP servers graph). Belongs in a deployment / orchestration product. The MCP-catalog cookbook recipe in Tier C is the only declarative slice scoped into the SDK; everything else stays Python-API.
  • HTTP service wrapper, readiness / liveness endpoints, K8s probes. Building a FastAPI / gRPC service around an Agent is application code. The SDK does not provide /health, /ready, or any HTTP surface, and 1.2.0 will not change that.
  • SSO / RBAC / multi-tenant audit at the SDK layer. Belongs in the surrounding deployment layer.
  • Process-level concerns — log shipping, secret-store integration with Vault / SSM / KMS as a service, queue workers, autoscalers. The SDK exposes hooks (middleware, SecretProvider) that an application can use to plug into these; it doesn't implement them.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Per-feature work
docs.text:
For every scope item picked in Phase 1:

  • [ ] Implement under kneo_agent/... with mypy --strict clean.
  • [ ] Tests in tests/unit/ (and tests/integration/ if it crosses a boundary). Aim for 100% on new code; global gate is 85%.
  • [ ] Runnable example in examples/NN_*.py or examples/cookbook/ if it's a user-facing primitive — the smoke test in tests/integration/test_examples.py will execute it (extend the smoke runner to walk cookbook/ if you add the directory).
  • [ ] Update public exports + __all__ in kneo_agent/__init__.py, and record the export-tier decision (top-level public / subpackage-only / experimental) in docs/api_stability.md.
  • [ ] Update the relevant section of docs/kneo_agent_api_reference.md so signatures, parameters, and examples in the manual stay in sync with the code in the same PR (the Phase 4 regeneration is then a no-op refresh, not a content rewrite).
  • [ ] Add an entry under [Unreleased] (Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed) in CHANGELOG.md.
  • [ ] If a new optional dep: add [extra] group in pyproject.toml, update [all], add a CI matrix combo in .github/workflows/ci.yml, document the pin-floor reason in CHANGELOG, expose a flag in install.sh.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Release mechanics
docs.text:
• [ ] Move [Unreleased] → ## [1.2.0] - YYYY-MM-DD in CHANGELOG.md.
  • [ ] Update the diff-link footer: v1.1.1...v1.2.0, [Unreleased]: ...compare/v1.2.0...HEAD.
  • [ ] Bump version = "1.1.1" → "1.2.0" in pyproject.toml.
  • [ ] Update banner Kneo Agent v1.1.1 → v1.2.0 in install.sh.
  • [ ] Update verify-import comment # → 1.1.1 → # → 1.2.0 in README.md and docs/README.md (after Phase 2).
  • [ ] Regenerate the API reference manual for v1.2.0 (docs/kneo_agent_api_reference.{md,html,pdf} via the existing docs/render_*.py / docs/render_pdf_with_header_footer.mjs toolchain). Update the cover, intro, footer, and Python-version banner from v1.1.1 / "Python 3.12+" to v1.2.0 / current floor. In the rendered HTML the version string currently appears at ~lines 783 (header), 907 (cover card), 1041 (intro badge), and 2546 (footer); regenerate from the Markdown source so all four update together. Verify every new or changed public primitive from Tier A/B/C is reflected (new middleware classes, base_url= parameters, formal RunResult.metadata["usage"] schema, MCP TLS knobs, workflow retry step, SecretProvider, etc.). The manual is advertised as the complete public-surface reference, so its accuracy is part of the release gate.
  • [ ] Doc / example drift gate. Run a docs-and-example link audit: every examples/... path mentioned in README.md, docs/README.md, the per-guide docs, and the regenerated API reference must (a) exist on disk and (b) either be exercised by tests/integration/test_examples.py or be explicitly skipped with a documented reason (the existing pattern for examples 12 and 13 — external resources required). Fold the audit into a one-shot script under tests/ so it stays useful past this release.
  • [ ] Local gate: ruff check kneo_agent/ tests/ && mypy kneo_agent/ && pytest -q tests --cov=kneo_agent --cov-fail-under=85
  • [ ] Local build + render check: python -m build && twine check dist/* (catches broken README rendering before tag push).
  • [ ] Commit, push to main.
  • [ ] TestPyPI dry-run: GitHub → Actions → Release → workflow_dispatch. Install from test.pypi in a clean venv; assert kneo_agent.__version__ == "1.2.0".
  • [ ] git tag v1.2.0 && git push --tags — Release workflow publishes to PyPI on tag push.
  • [ ] Approve the pypi environment in Actions if required-reviewers is enabled.

docs.title: kneo-agent 1.2.0
docs.text:
A backwards-compatible minor release focused on production reliability, on-prem deployment, and enterprise data-source integration through the SDK's existing tools and MCP surface. Every public name from 1.1.x still works the same way.

pip install --upgrade kneo-agent is safe — read docs/upgrading_to_1.2.md for a code-level walkthrough of what's new.

docs.title: 🏠 Run on local LLMs
docs.text:
First-class base_url= / api_key= on every OpenAI entry point. Point at Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, or LocalAI in one call:

from kneo_agent import build_sync_agent

agent = build_sync_agent(
    "openai",
    base_url="http://localhost:11434/v1",
    model="llama3.1",
    system_prompt="You are a concise assistant.",
)

docs.title: 🛡️ Production middleware bundle
docs.text:
New kneo_agent.middleware subpackage — drop-in, stdlib-only:

  • RetryMiddleware — exponential backoff + jitter
  • RateLimitMiddleware — token-bucket throttle
  • TokenBudgetMiddleware — per-run / cumulative caps from RunResult.metadata["usage"]
  • RedactionMiddleware — regex scrubbing with a COMMON_PATTERNS starter pack

docs.title: 🔐 Secrets without leaks

from kneo_agent.utils import EnvSecretProvider, FileSecretProvider

# K8s/Docker secret-mount pattern
secrets = FileSecretProvider("/var/run/secrets/myapp")
api_token = secrets.get("api_token")

    client_cert="/etc/ssl/corp/client.crt",

docs.title: Agent Middleware Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how middleware works in kneo_agent.

docs.title: What Middleware Is For
docs.text:
Middleware is the SDK's cross-cutting interception layer. It is useful for:

  • logging and tracing
  • guardrails and policy enforcement
  • request or response mutation
  • tool result rewriting
  • short-circuiting runs or streams

The design combines two ideas:

  • shared mutable context objects
  • phase-specific hooks around the agent loop

docs.title: Supported Hook Points
docs.text:
kneo_agent exposes four middleware hooks:

  • wrap_run(context, handler) for Agent.run(...)
  • wrap_stream(context, handler) for Agent.stream(...)
  • wrap_model_call(context, handler) for one Bridge executor model call
  • wrap_tool_call(context, handler) for one Bridge executor tool dispatch

wrap_run(...) and wrap_stream(...) apply to every runtime style.

wrap_model_call(...) and wrap_tool_call(...) apply only to Bridge runtimes, because Kneo owns the inner loop there.

docs.title: Static vs Per-Run Middleware
docs.text:
Attach middleware statically at build time:

from kneo_agent import AgentBuilder, BaseAgentMiddleware


class LoggingMiddleware(BaseAgentMiddleware):
    async def wrap_run(self, context, handler):
        print(f"running {context.agent_name}")
        return await handler(context)


agent = (
    AgentBuilder()
    .add_middleware(LoggingMiddleware())
    .use_runtime(runtime)
    .build()
)

Attach middleware for a single invocation:

from kneo_agent import RunConfig

result = await agent.run(
    "hello",
    run_config=RunConfig(middlewares=[LoggingMiddleware()]),
)

Per-run middleware is appended after statically configured middleware, so the per-run middleware executes deeper in the chain.

docs.title: Shared Mutable Context
docs.text:
Each hook receives a context object with the current request state and a handler function that delegates to the next middleware or terminal runtime operation.

Middleware can:

  • mutate context.messages
  • replace or augment context.run_config
  • add values to context.metadata
  • return early without calling handler(...)

docs.title: Short-Circuiting
docs.text:
Middleware may skip the rest of the pipeline entirely.

That is useful for:

  • blocked requests
  • cached answers
  • synthetic previews
  • fallback behavior

docs.title: Relationship To Skills
docs.text:
Skills and middleware are complementary but different:

  • skills package reusable data such as prompts, tools, defaults, and metadata
  • middleware is executable code that wraps runtime behavior

Skills compile into RunConfig. Middleware remains an explicit object attached through AgentBuilder or RunConfig.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
kneo_agent.observability.OpenTelemetryMiddleware is a built-in middleware that emits spans following the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions. Spans are named chat <agent> for runs, chat iter=<n> for Bridge model calls, and execute_tool <name> for tool executions, with attributes including gen_ai.system, gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.agent.name, gen_ai.tool.name, and gen_ai.usage.{input,output}_tokens when the runtime surfaces token counts via RunResult.metadata["usage"].

Install the optional extra:

pip install "kneo-agent[telemetry]"

Wire it up like any other middleware:

from kneo_agent import AgentBuilder
from kneo_agent.observability import OpenTelemetryMiddleware

agent = (
    AgentBuilder()
    .add_middleware(OpenTelemetryMiddleware())
    .use_bridge(runtime)
    .build()
)

Pass record_arguments=False to suppress tool-call argument capture when inputs may contain PII. Pass record_results=True to also attach tool results to spans.

docs.title: Production middleware bundle (v1.2.0)
docs.text:
kneo_agent.middleware ships four production-grade middleware classes built on the framework above. Use them as drop-ins:

from kneo_agent.middleware import (
    RetryMiddleware,
    RateLimitMiddleware,
    TokenBudgetMiddleware,
    RedactionMiddleware,
    COMMON_PATTERNS,
)
Middleware What it does RetryMiddleware Retries wrap_model_call and wrap_tool_call with exponential backoff + jitter. Configurable retry_on; never retries asyncio.CancelledError. RateLimitMiddleware Token-bucket throttle. scope="run" (default) limits whole runs; scope="model_call" limits Bridge model calls. TokenBudgetMiddleware Enforces per-run and / or cumulative token caps from RunResult.metadata["usage"]. Raises TokenBudgetExceeded. RedactionMiddleware Regex scrubbing of secrets in inputs, tool args, tool results, the final result, and streamed chunks. Ships a COMMON_PATTERNS starter pack (Bearer / JWT / AWS / OpenAI / connection-string shapes).

Recommended ordering when combined with observability:

  1. RedactionMiddleware — registered first (outer) so input is scrubbed before any inner middleware sees it.
  2. OpenTelemetryMiddleware(record_arguments=True, record_results=False) — inner. record_results=False keeps un-redacted output out of spans.

The framework types (AgentMiddleware, BaseAgentMiddleware, the four context dataclasses) are re-exported from kneo_agent.middleware, so a single import line gives you both the framework and the bundle.

For credential plumbing through tool handlers and MCP transports without leaking values into prompts or trace spans, pair RedactionMiddleware with the SecretProvider Protocol in kneo_agent.utils (see api_stability.md and upgrading_to_1.2.md).

docs.title: Agent Skills Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how kneo_agent integrates with the Agent Skills open standard from agentskills.io.

docs.title: What Kneo Supports
docs.text:
Kneo Agent supports two skill authoring paths:

  1. In-memory skills created directly in Python with Skill(...) or ToolRegistry.to_skill(...)
  2. Disk-backed skills loaded from Agent Skills-compatible SKILL.md directories

The second path is designed to interoperate with the broader Agent Skills ecosystem.

Skills work alongside middleware, but they solve different problems:

  • skills package reusable prompts, tools, defaults, and metadata
  • middleware adds executable policy around runs, streams, model calls, and tool calls

docs.title: Supported File Structure
docs.text:
Kneo Agent expects either:

  • A path to a skill directory containing SKILL.md
  • A direct path to SKILL.md

Example:

weather/
├── SKILL.md
├── references/
│   └── REFERENCE.md
├── scripts/
│   └── normalize_weather.py
└── assets/

docs.title: SKILL.md Format
docs.text:
SKILL.md must contain:

  • YAML frontmatter delimited by ---
  • A Markdown body used as the skill instruction content

Minimum required frontmatter fields:

  • name
  • description

Kneo Agent also preserves these optional fields when present:

  • license
  • compatibility
  • metadata
  • allowed-tools
  • tools
  • defaults
  • extra
  • tags

Example:

---
name: weather
description: Load a reusable weather skill from disk and use it for weather questions.
license: MIT
compatibility: Works with Python and a registered get_weather handler.
metadata:
  author: kneo-agent
allowed-tools: Bash(python:*) Read
tools:
  - name: get_weather
    description: Return current weather for a city.
    parameters:
      type: object
      properties:
        city:
          type: string
      required:
        - city
defaults:
  max_iterations: 5
tags:
  - domain:weather
---

# Weather Skill

Use this skill when the user asks for current weather conditions by city.

docs.title: Loading Skills
docs.text:
Use load_skill(...) to activate a single skill:

from kneo_agent import load_skill

skill = load_skill("examples/skills/weather")

If the skill declares tools, bind handlers in code:

skill = skill.with_tool_handlers({"get_weather": get_weather})

That split is deliberate: the standard file defines portable metadata and instructions, while executable handlers stay local to the host application.

docs.title: Discovering Skills
docs.text:
Use discover_skills(...) to scan one or more directories:

from kneo_agent import discover_skills

catalog = discover_skills(["examples/skills"])
for entry in catalog:
    print(entry.name, entry.path)

Use discover_default_skills(...) to scan conventional locations:

from kneo_agent import discover_default_skills

catalog = discover_default_skills(
    project_root=".",
    user_home="~",
)

The default search covers:

  • .agents/skills
  • .claude/skills

docs.title: Progressive Disclosure
docs.text:
Kneo Agent supports the Agent Skills guidance to keep SKILL.md concise and place detailed material in sibling folders.

Supported bundled resource folders:

  • references/
  • scripts/
  • assets/

Resources are discoverable but not injected automatically into every run.

Use:

paths = skill.resource_paths()
reference_text = skill.read_resource("references/REFERENCE.md")

This keeps the core skill lightweight while still letting the runtime or host agent load extra material on demand.

docs.title: Activation Payloads
docs.text:
For integrations that want to inject a structured skill payload into prompts, use:

prompt = skill.activation_prompt()

This returns:

  • The Markdown body from SKILL.md
  • The skill directory path
  • A list of discoverable bundled resources

docs.title: Current Kneo Behavior
docs.text:
Kneo Agent currently maps Agent Skills into its existing runtime contract:

  • The Markdown body becomes Skill.system_prompt
  • Frontmatter tools becomes ToolDefinition[]
  • Frontmatter defaults contributes to RunConfig
  • Frontmatter extra merges into RunConfig.extra
  • Bound tool handlers are merged into extra["tool_handlers"]

This means skills work across Bridge, Native, and Adapter runtimes without provider-specific changes.

Middleware is intentionally separate from this mapping. Skills compile into data-oriented RunConfig fields, while middleware remains executable code attached explicitly through AgentBuilder or RunConfig(middlewares=[...]).

docs.title: MCP-Backed Tool Registries
docs.text:
MCP support builds on the same capability path rather than introducing a separate execution model.

A typical pattern is:

  1. import remote MCP tools into ToolRegistry
  2. package that registry into a skill or attach it with AgentBuilder.with_tool_registry(...)
  3. let the existing RunConfig.extra["tool_handlers"] mechanism execute them

Example:

from kneo_agent import MCPServerConfig
from kneo_agent.utils import ToolRegistry

registry = ToolRegistry()
await registry.register_mcp_server(
    MCPServerConfig.stdio(
        name="filesystem",
        command="npx",
        args=["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/tmp"],
    ),
    prefix="fs_",
)

skill = registry.to_skill("filesystem-mcp")

This keeps MCP tool servers aligned with the same skill and tool packaging model described in the rest of this guide.

docs.title: API Stability and Deprecation Policy
docs.text: kneo-agent follows Semantic Versioning on the public surface defined below. This page tells you what you can pin, what you can rely on across upgrades, and how deprecations are communicated.

docs.title: What counts as public surface
docs.text:
A name is public if it satisfies all of these:

  1. It is listed in kneo_agent.__all__ (top-level package), or in the __all__ of one of the documented subpackages (kneo_agent.core, kneo_agent.patterns, kneo_agent.providers, kneo_agent.runtime, kneo_agent.workflows, kneo_agent.utils, kneo_agent.mcp, kneo_agent.observability, kneo_agent.middleware).
  2. It is documented in the rendered API reference (docs/pub/kneo_agent_api_reference.html / .pdf).
  3. It is not marked experimental (see below).

The set of public names is pinned by tests/unit/test_public_api_snapshot.py. A change to that snapshot must land in the same PR as the matching CHANGELOG.md entry and the API-reference update.

Anything else — modules, classes, functions whose name begins with _, attributes only reachable via implementation paths — is internal. It can change without notice between any two releases, including patch releases. Don't import it.

docs.title: Stable (default)
docs.text:
Public names ship under SemVer. You can pin to a minor version range (kneo-agent ~= 1.2) and trust that:

  • No public name in __all__ is removed within a minor line.
  • No public function or method drops a parameter, narrows a type, or changes a documented return shape within a minor line.
  • New public names, new optional parameters, and additive type-widening changes ship in minor releases (1.2.0 → 1.3.0).
  • Breaking changes — removing names, renaming parameters, narrowing return types — only ship in major releases (1.x → 2.0).

docs.title: Experimental
docs.text:
Some new APIs ship marked experimental so we can iterate without charging the deprecation tax. Experimental names:

  • Are flagged in their docstring with .. note:: Experimental — interface may change in any release.
  • Are flagged with the same wording in their CHANGELOG entry.
  • Are flagged in the API reference manual.
  • Can change shape or be removed in any release (including patch) until they are graduated to stable. Graduation lands in a minor release with a CHANGELOG entry that says "Graduated from experimental to stable".

    If you depend on an experimental API in production, pin to an exact version (kneo-agent == 1.2.3).

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text:
When we need to remove a stable name, it goes through a deprecation window:

  1. Mark deprecated — the name still works and behaves the same, but emits DeprecationWarning on use. The CHANGELOG entry announces the deprecation, the replacement (if any), and the target removal version. The API reference flags the name with a Deprecated since X.Y.0 note.
  2. Grace window — the name is preserved through the next minor release at minimum. So a deprecation announced in 1.2.0 is only eligible for removal in 1.4.0 or later (not 1.3.0).
  3. Remove in a major release — actual removal happens in the next major bump (2.0). For long-lived APIs we may extend the grace window further.

Tests in tests/unit/ cover deprecated names with two assertions: (a) calling the name emits DeprecationWarning, and (b) the documented behavior still works.

docs.title: What's not covered
docs.text:
Behavior outside SemVer guarantees, even if you can observe it:

  • Internal module layouts (anything under kneo_agent.providers.<provider>.* not re-exported from kneo_agent.providers).
  • Tool dispatch ordering beyond the documented "static-then-per-run" middleware chain.
  • Log message formats and logger names.
  • Wire formats of provider SDKs we wrap (those are upstream).
  • Optional dependency floor versions — these can move within a minor line if upstream forces a security or compatibility fix.
  • Telemetry attribute values beyond the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-convention keys we explicitly map.

docs.title: Reporting drift
docs.text: If you spot a public name that changed without a CHANGELOG entry, or an experimental name without the experimental marker, please open an issue. Drift in either direction is a bug.

docs.title: Human In The Loop Guide
docs.text:
This guide explains how kneo_agent supports human review steps inside workflows.

Middleware and human-in-the-loop are complementary:

  • middleware is best for automated policy, logging, or short-circuiting
  • human steps are best when a real person must approve, edit, or pause execution

docs.title: Core Idea
docs.text:
Human-in-the-loop support is modeled as a normal workflow participant.

That keeps the design aligned with the rest of the workflow system:

  • agents can draft or analyze
  • function steps can transform
  • human steps can approve, reject, edit, or pause execution

The main API is WorkflowBuilder.human_step(...).

docs.title: Inline Resolver
docs.text:
Use an inline resolver when your application can obtain human input during the same workflow run.

from kneo_agent.workflows import WorkflowBuilder

review = WorkflowBuilder.human_step(
    "approval",
    "Approve this draft?",
    resolver=lambda request: "Approved by Alice",
)

The resolver receives a HumanInterventionRequest containing:

  • step_name
  • prompt
  • the current messages
  • the active RunConfig
  • any workflow metadata attached to the step

If the resolver returns a string, that string is appended as a human message and the workflow continues.

docs.title: Pause / Escalation Mode
docs.text:
If no resolver is provided, or if the resolver returns None, the workflow raises HumanInterventionRequiredError.

from kneo_agent import HumanInterventionRequiredError

try:
    await workflow.run(messages, config)
except HumanInterventionRequiredError as exc:
    print(exc.step_name)
    print(exc.prompt)
    print(exc.request)

This is the right fit when your host application needs to:

  • pause execution
  • show a review UI
  • collect approval from a person later
  • resume the broader process in a separate request or session

docs.title: Graph And Sequential Workflows
docs.text:
Human steps work anywhere a workflow participant can appear:

  • SequentialWorkflow
  • graph Workflow
  • nested workflows
  • handoff, concurrent, or group-chat orchestrations

Example:

workflow = WorkflowBuilder.sequential(
    [
        writer,
        WorkflowBuilder.human_step(
            "editor_review",
            lambda messages, config: f"Approve this draft? {messages[-1].content}",
            resolver=lambda request: "Approved",
        ),
        publish_step,
    ],
    name="release-workflow",
)

docs.title: MCP Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how kneo_agent integrates with MCP tool servers.

docs.title: What MCP Means In Kneo Agent
docs.text:
Kneo Agent treats an MCP server as an external tool source.

The flow is:

  1. Connect to an MCP server with MCPServerConfig
  2. Discover remote tools with ToolRegistry.register_mcp_server(...)
  3. Convert those tools into normal ToolDefinition objects plus proxy handlers
  4. Package the registry into an agent with AgentBuilder.with_tool_registry(...)

That means MCP support does not require a new runtime type. Bridge, Native, and Adapter runtimes can all use MCP tools through the existing RunConfig and tool_handlers path.

Middleware composes with MCP naturally:

  • use run middleware for tracing, guardrails, or request shaping
  • use Bridge tool-call middleware when you want to inspect or rewrite MCP tool results before they are fed back into the loop

docs.title: Supported Transports
docs.text:
Kneo Agent supports three MCP connection styles:

  • stdio: launch a subprocess and speak JSON-RPC over standard I/O
  • http: send JSON-RPC requests to an HTTP endpoint
  • sse: listen on an SSE stream and send JSON-RPC requests to a message endpoint

docs.title: Stdio Example
docs.text:
import asyncio
from kneo_agent import AgentBuilder, MCPServerConfig
from kneo_agent.patterns import NativeRuntimeFactory
from kneo_agent.utils import ToolRegistry


async def main() -> None:
    registry = ToolRegistry()
    await registry.register_mcp_server(
        MCPServerConfig.stdio(
            name="filesystem",
            command="npx",
            args=["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/tmp"],
        ),
        prefix="fs_",
    )

    runtime = NativeRuntimeFactory.for_openai(model="gpt-4o", strategy="react")
    agent = (
        AgentBuilder()
        .with_name("Filesystem Assistant")
        .with_tool_registry(registry, skill_name="filesystem-mcp")
        .use_runtime(runtime)
        .build()
    )

    print(await agent.chat("List the files in /tmp."))
    await registry.aclose()


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: HTTP Example
docs.text:
config = MCPServerConfig.http(
    name="remote-http",
    url="https://example.com/mcp",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer <token>"},
)

docs.title: SSE Example
docs.text:
config = MCPServerConfig.sse(
    name="remote-sse",
    sse_url="https://example.com/mcp/events",
    message_url="https://example.com/mcp/messages",
)

For SSE, some servers publish the message endpoint through the event stream. If yours does, message_url can be omitted.

docs.title: TLS / mTLS / custom CA (v1.2.0)
docs.text:
Both MCPServerConfig.http() and .sse() accept TLS knobs for on-prem deployments behind corporate certificate authorities or with mutual-TLS requirements:

config = MCPServerConfig.http(
    name="internal",
    url="https://mcp.internal.corp/v1",
    headers={"X-Internal-Auth": "..."},
    ca_bundle="/etc/ssl/corp/ca.pem",       # custom root CA
    client_cert="/etc/ssl/corp/client.crt", # client cert for mTLS
    client_key="/etc/ssl/corp/client.key",  # matching key
)
Parameter Purpose verify Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate. Default True; set False only for development against a known-bad self-signed cert. ca_bundle Path to a PEM-encoded CA bundle. Use this for corporate or internal CAs that aren't in the system trust store. client_cert Path to a PEM-encoded client certificate for mTLS. client_key Path to the client certificate's private key. Required when client_cert is set unless the cert file already contains the key.

The transports build an ssl.SSLContext from these knobs and thread it into urlopen(..., context=...). Apps that need to inspect or share the context can call MCPServerConfig.build_ssl_context() directly — it returns None when no TLS customization is requested (the default-trust-store case).

For loading a list of internal MCP servers from a YAML/JSON config at app startup, see examples/cookbook/mcp_server_catalog.py.

docs.title: Working With ToolRegistry
docs.text:
ToolRegistry.register_mcp_server(...) returns a list of discovered ToolDefinition objects and registers callable proxies for each one.

tools = await registry.register_mcp_server(config, prefix="remote_")
print([tool.name for tool in tools])

Use prefix when you want to namespace a server's tools locally and avoid name collisions with other MCP servers or local Python tools.

When you are done, close the registry to clean up subprocesses and sessions:

await registry.aclose()

docs.title: Working With AgentBuilder
docs.text:
The easiest way to expose MCP tools to an agent is:

agent = (
    AgentBuilder()
    .with_name("MCP Assistant")
    .with_tool_registry(registry, skill_name="mcp-tools")
    .use_runtime(runtime)
    .build()
)

with_tool_registry(...) does two things:

  • copies registry.definitions into the agent's tool list
  • packages the registry handlers into an implicit Skill

That keeps MCP integration aligned with the existing skill/tool resolution pipeline.

docs.title: Offline / air-gapped install
docs.text: kneo-agent is a pure-Python library that does not phone home and does not require network access at runtime — beyond whatever your own application chooses to talk to. This page explains how to install it on a host with no outbound internet, and what that means for your audit story.

docs.title: No phone-home guarantee
docs.text:
The SDK does not perform analytics, telemetry, update checks, or "call home" requests of any kind. The only outbound network calls the SDK can make are:

  1. Provider SDK calls through the optional extras (openai-agents, langchain, google-adk). These only trigger when your code invokes an agent that uses those extras, and they go to the endpoints your code configured (e.g. base_url=... for a local Ollama).
  2. MCP HTTP / SSE transports (MCPServerConfig.http() / .sse()). These only trigger when your code registers an MCP server.

The [telemetry] extra ships only opentelemetry-api, which has no exporter — your deployment chooses where to ship spans (none, a local OTLP collector, etc.). See self_hosted_observability.md.

For a code-level audit, grep for outbound calls in kneo_agent/ — you will find urllib.request.urlopen only inside kneo_agent/mcp/client.py (the MCP transports) and nothing else.

docs.title: Installing in an air-gapped environment
docs.text: The standard pattern: download wheels on a connected host, transfer them to the air-gapped host, install with --no-index --find-links.

docs.title: 1. On a connected host
docs.text:
# Choose the same Python version + platform as the target host.
# --platform / --python-version match what `pip install` would
# resolve on the target.
mkdir -p wheelhouse
pip download \
    --dest wheelhouse \
    --python-version 3.12 \
    --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 \
    --only-binary=:all: \
    "kneo-agent[all]==1.2.0"

Adjust --platform for your target (e.g. manylinux_2_28_x86_64, macosx_14_0_arm64). Drop [all] to omit provider extras you don't need; the matching set keeps only core + PyYAML.

docs.title: 2. Transfer the wheelhouse
docs.text: rsync, scp, USB, whatever your security model requires. The wheelhouse is just a directory of .whl and .tar.gz files — nothing in it executes during transfer.

docs.title: 3. On the air-gapped host
docs.text:
python -m venv /opt/myapp/venv
source /opt/myapp/venv/bin/activate
pip install --no-index --find-links /path/to/wheelhouse \
    "kneo-agent[all]==1.2.0"

--no-index tells pip not to consult any package index; --find-links points it at the local directory. If the resolver complains about a missing dependency, your pip download step on the connected host missed it — re-run pip download with the same flags as your target install, or add the missing package name explicitly.

docs.title: 4. Verify
docs.text:
python -c "import kneo_agent; print(kneo_agent.__version__)"
# → 1.2.0

For the no-phone-home guarantee, smoke-test on a host with no outbound network at all:

# Block all egress (example with iptables; adjust for your platform).
sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -j REJECT
python -c "
from kneo_agent import AgentBuilder
agent = AgentBuilder().with_name('air-gap').build()
print(agent)
"

Importing the SDK and constructing an Agent (without invoking a provider) makes zero outbound calls.

docs.title: Reproducible installs
docs.text:
For audit-grade reproducibility:

pip download --dest wheelhouse \
    --no-deps \
    "kneo-agent==1.2.0"
pip download --dest wheelhouse "kneo-agent==1.2.0"   # then resolve deps
sha256sum wheelhouse/* > wheelhouse.SHA256SUMS

Verify on the target host:

sha256sum -c wheelhouse.SHA256SUMS

If your release pipeline already produces a manifest, use that as the source of truth — kneo-agent has nothing kneo-specific to add beyond standard pip-wheel discipline.

docs.title: Updating in place
docs.text:
Because the SDK does not check for updates, upgrading is entirely your call. Re-run the pip download step on a connected host against the new version, transfer, and re-install with --no-index --find-links against the new wheelhouse.

The upgrading_to_1.2.md guide covers the user-facing changes between minor releases.

docs.title: What you still need network access to (just not from the SDK itself)
docs.text:
• Whatever LLM provider your agent talks to (a local Ollama / vLLM / llama.cpp server is fine; that's still on-prem).
  • Whatever MCP servers your agent uses (MCPServerConfig can point at a localhost URL — no public network needed).
  • Whatever observability backend your application ships spans to (a local OTLP collector / Jaeger / Tempo / SigNoz — see self_hosted_observability.md).

The library installs and runs without any of those. They become required only when your application code chooses to use them.

docs.title: Self-hosted observability
docs.text:
kneo-agent ships an OpenTelemetryMiddleware that emits GenAI semantic-convention spans. The SDK does not bundle an exporter — that's a deployment concern your application owns. This guide shows how to wire the middleware to common self-hostable backends: OTLP collector, Jaeger, Grafana Tempo, and SigNoz.

The kneo-agent side is identical for all four — the only thing that changes is which container you point the exporter at.

docs.title: 1. Install the telemetry extra
docs.text:
pip install "kneo-agent[telemetry]"
pip install opentelemetry-sdk opentelemetry-exporter-otlp

The [telemetry] extra brings in opentelemetry-api only, on purpose — it's the part the SDK uses. The exporter (-otlp, -jaeger, -zipkin, …) is a deployment choice, so apps install it explicitly.

docs.title: 2. Attach the middleware
docs.text:
Wire it into your agent the same way as any other middleware:

from kneo_agent import build_agent
from kneo_agent.observability import OpenTelemetryMiddleware

agent = build_agent(
    "openai",
    base_url="http://localhost:11434/v1",
    model="llama3.1",
    middlewares=[
        OpenTelemetryMiddleware(
            record_arguments=True,    # set False to suppress tool-arg attrs
            record_results=False,     # set False to suppress final-result attrs
        ),
    ],
)

Pair it with RedactionMiddleware if your inputs may contain secrets — see api_stability.md and the kneo_agent.middleware package docstring for the recommended ordering (Redaction outer, OTel inner; record_results=False keeps un-redacted output out of spans).

docs.title: 3. Configure the SDK exporter
docs.text:
This is standard OpenTelemetry; the SDK doesn't get involved. Recommended: configure it once at app startup before any agent runs.

from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.http.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter

provider = TracerProvider()
provider.add_span_processor(
    BatchSpanProcessor(
        OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint="http://localhost:4318/v1/traces")
    )
)
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)

Switch to gRPC by importing from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter and using the :4317 port.

docs.title: 4. Backend recipes
docs.text: Run any of these alongside your application; pick one and point the OTLP exporter at it. None of them are an SDK artifact — they're infrastructure your application's deployment pulls in.

docs.title: OTLP collector (vendor-neutral)
docs.text:
# docker-compose.yml
services:
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest
    command: ["--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml"]
    volumes:
      - ./otel-config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # gRPC
      - "4318:4318"   # HTTP

# otel-config.yaml — minimal: receive OTLP, log to stdout
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
      http:
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [debug]
exporters:
  debug:
    verbosity: detailed

docs.title: Jaeger (all-in-one)
docs.text:
services:
  jaeger:
    image: jaegertracing/all-in-one:latest
    environment:
      - COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true
    ports:
      - "16686:16686"  # UI
      - "4317:4317"    # OTLP gRPC
      - "4318:4318"    # OTLP HTTP

Open http://localhost:16686 for the Jaeger UI. The kneo-agent spans appear under service name kneo_agent (the default span attribute set by OpenTelemetryMiddleware).

docs.title: Grafana Tempo + Grafana
docs.text:
services:
  tempo:
    image: grafana/tempo:latest
    command: ["-config.file=/etc/tempo.yaml"]
    volumes:
      - ./tempo.yaml:/etc/tempo.yaml
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"
      - "4318:4318"
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:latest
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"

Point Grafana's data source at http://tempo:3200 and query the GenAI semantic-convention attributes:

  • gen_ai.system
  • gen_ai.operation.name
  • gen_ai.agent.name
  • gen_ai.tool.name
  • gen_ai.usage.input_tokens / gen_ai.usage.output_tokens

docs.title: SigNoz
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz.git
cd signoz/deploy
./install.sh

SigNoz exposes an OTLP receiver on :4317 (gRPC) and :4318 (HTTP). Open http://localhost:3301 for the SigNoz UI.

docs.title: 5. Verify end-to-end
docs.text:
A minimal smoke check that doesn't require a real LLM:

import asyncio
from kneo_agent import build_agent
from kneo_agent.observability import OpenTelemetryMiddleware

# Configure the exporter as in step 3 first.

async def main():
    agent = build_agent(
        "openai",
        base_url="http://localhost:11434/v1",   # your local server
        model="llama3.1",
        middlewares=[OpenTelemetryMiddleware()],
    )
    print(await agent.chat("ping"))

asyncio.run(main())

Within ~30 seconds, the run should appear in your chosen backend under the kneo_agent service. The middleware emits one span per agent run plus child spans for tool calls and model invocations when those flow through the Bridge runtime.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• No spans appear. Check the exporter is configured before any agent runs (the TracerProvider is read at first use). Run with OTEL_LOG_LEVEL=debug set to surface exporter errors on stderr.
  • Spans missing usage attributes. Only the OpenAI Agents native runtime populates RunResult.metadata["usage"] in 1.2.0; on other runtimes the OTel middleware has nothing to copy. Populate via custom middleware or wait for the per-runtime rollout in a follow-up release.
  • TLS errors against an internal collector. The exporter is a standard OpenTelemetry component — configure its CA bundle the same way you would for any other Python HTTP client (env vars like REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / SSL_CERT_FILE, or OTLPSpanExporter(certificate_file=...)).

docs.title: Upgrading to 1.2.0
docs.text: A short, practical "should I upgrade?" walkthrough for users on 1.1.x. The full list of changes is in CHANGELOG.md; this page covers only the parts that affect existing code.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
• No breaking changes. Every public name from 1.1.x still works the same way. New features are additive. You can pip install --upgrade kneo-agent and run your existing code unchanged.
  • Worth upgrading for: local-LLM support without pre-building an AsyncOpenAI client; the new middleware bundle (retry / rate-limit / token-budget / redaction); a documented RunResult.metadata["usage"] schema; MCP TLS / mTLS support; and a SecretProvider Protocol with three reference implementations.
  • Read this page first if you: pin to a specific subpackage size, pass MCP servers behind a corporate CA, or care about the RunResult.metadata shape.

docs.title: 1. Local LLMs via base_url=
docs.text:
Before 1.2.0 you had to pre-build an AsyncOpenAI client to point at Ollama / vLLM / llama.cpp / LocalAI. Now base_url= and api_key= are first-class on every OpenAI entry point:

from kneo_agent import build_sync_agent

agent = build_sync_agent(
    "openai",
    base_url="http://localhost:11434/v1",
    model="llama3.1",
    system_prompt="You are a concise assistant.",
)

The same parameters land on BridgeAgentFactory.for_openai, NativeRuntimeFactory.for_openai, and OpenAIAgentsImpl. Passing both openai_client= and base_url= raises ValueError.

When base_url is set without api_key, the SDK uses a placeholder string so AsyncOpenAI doesn't error on a missing key (most local servers ignore it). Set api_key= explicitly when your local server checks it.

See examples/cookbook/local_ollama.py for a runnable demo.

docs.title: 2. Middleware bundle (kneo_agent.middleware)
docs.text:
Four new middlewares ship under a new subpackage:

from kneo_agent.middleware import (
    RetryMiddleware,
    RateLimitMiddleware,
    TokenBudgetMiddleware,
    RedactionMiddleware,
    COMMON_PATTERNS,
)
  • RetryMiddleware — retries transient model / tool failures with exponential backoff; never retries asyncio.CancelledError.
  • RateLimitMiddleware — token-bucket throttle on whole runs or individual model calls.
  • TokenBudgetMiddleware — per-run / cumulative caps from RunResult.metadata["usage"]. Raises TokenBudgetExceeded.
  • RedactionMiddleware — regex scrubbing of secrets in inputs, tool args, tool results, the final result, and streamed chunks. Ships a COMMON_PATTERNS starter pack.

The framework types (AgentMiddleware, BaseAgentMiddleware, the context dataclasses) are re-exported from kneo_agent.middleware, so you can import everything from one place.

Ordering rule (covered in detail in the package docstring):

  1. Static middleware (registered via AgentBuilder.add_middleware) wraps every run, in registration order.
  2. Per-run middleware (passed via RunConfig.middlewares) is appended inside the static list.

For redaction + observability specifically: register RedactionMiddleware outer (first via add_middleware) and OpenTelemetryMiddleware(record_results=False) inner. The redaction layer scrubs inputs before the OTel layer records them, and record_results=False keeps un-redacted output out of the spans.

docs.title: 3. Documented RunResult.metadata["usage"] schema
docs.text:
The usage key on RunResult.metadata now has a formal shape:

{
    "input_tokens": int,
    "output_tokens": int,
    "total_tokens": int,           # equals input + output
}

prompt_tokens / completion_tokens are accepted as aliases for provider-native naming.

Population today: the OpenAI Agents native runtime (for_openai in both NativeRuntimeFactory and BridgeAgentFactory) populates metadata["usage"] automatically by summing across raw_responses[*].usage. LangChain, Google ADK, and Bridge runtimes do not yet populate it; if you need usage tracking on those paths, populate metadata["usage"] from a custom middleware. The full docstring on RunResult enumerates which runtimes do and don't populate.

OpenTelemetryMiddleware reads the documented keys and emits the GenAI semantic-convention attributes gen_ai.usage.input_tokens / gen_ai.usage.output_tokens. TokenBudgetMiddleware reads the same keys to enforce caps.

docs.title: 4. MCP TLS / mTLS / custom CA
docs.text:
MCPServerConfig.http() and .sse() now accept TLS knobs:

from kneo_agent import MCPServerConfig

config = MCPServerConfig.http(
    name="internal",
    url="https://mcp.internal.corp/v1",
    ca_bundle="/etc/ssl/corp/ca.pem",
    client_cert="/etc/ssl/corp/client.crt",
    client_key="/etc/ssl/corp/client.key",
    headers={"X-Internal-Auth": "..."},
)

MCPServerConfig.build_ssl_context() returns the corresponding ssl.SSLContext; both transports thread it into urlopen(..., context=...). No code change is needed if you were already on the public CA path.

docs.title: 5. SecretProvider Protocol
docs.text:
kneo_agent.utils now exports a SecretProvider Protocol plus three reference implementations:

from kneo_agent.utils import (
    EnvSecretProvider,       # env vars with optional prefix
    FileSecretProvider,      # K8s/Docker secret-mount file pattern
    MappingSecretProvider,   # in-memory dict for tests
    SecretProvider,
    SecretNotFound,
)

The SDK does not auto-resolve secrets — it documents one well-known shape so applications plumb credentials through their tool handlers and MCP transports without embedding raw strings in prompts or tool args. The Protocol is runtime_checkable, so isinstance(my_vault_provider, SecretProvider) works against your own implementation.

Pair with RedactionMiddleware for defense in depth.

docs.title: 6. Workflow retry-on-failure
docs.text:
kneo_agent.workflows.RetryStep wraps any WorkflowComponent (an Agent, FunctionStep, or nested Workflow) with retry semantics. Mirrors the middleware version; preserves the inner component's name so existing graph edges still match.

from kneo_agent.workflows import RetryStep, WorkflowBuilder

builder = WorkflowBuilder(RetryStep(prepare, max_attempts=3))
builder.add_executor(RetryStep(call_provider, max_attempts=5,
                               retry_on=(ConnectionError,)))

WorkflowBuilder.add_edge(..., condition=...) and WorkflowEdge.condition were already available in 1.1.x — see examples/cookbook/workflow_branching_and_retry.py for a full graph example. There is no separate WorkflowGraphBuilder class — WorkflowBuilder is the graph builder.

docs.title: 7. Sync-API failure-mode callout
docs.text: The build_sync_agent / SyncAgent failure mode (raises RuntimeError inside an already-running event loop — Jupyter, FastAPI handler, other async code) is now documented in three places: README, docs/README.md, and the API reference manual. No code change.

docs.title: 8. Python 3.13 classifier
docs.text: Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13 is now in pyproject.toml classifiers. CI was already exercising 3.13 in 1.1.x.

docs.title: What didn't change
docs.text:
• The top-level kneo_agent.__all__ set (75 names) is unchanged. A new snapshot test (tests/unit/test_public_api_snapshot.py) pins this surface so future drift fails CI.
  • The AgentMiddleware Protocol and four hooks (wrap_run, wrap_stream, wrap_model_call, wrap_tool_call) are unchanged.
  • The provider-extra version floors are unchanged.

docs.title: What's still pending
docs.text:
The following items from the v1.2.0 roadmap landed in design / docs but did not land in the SDK code:

  • Usage population for LangChain / Google ADK / Bridge runtimes. Documented in the RunResult docstring as not-yet-populated; apps that need this should populate via custom middleware.
  • Enterprise data-source tool recipes (SQL / object store / REST / search). The cookbook structure is in place; the recipes themselves are tracked for a follow-up release.
